record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; contents of the listed results files were not provided.
record.tranche_reason: The repository description reports that the refusal direction is redundant and low-dimensional, and causal but ineffective as a guardrail. These statements refine or qualify the single-direction claim, but no experimental details are available.
record.gate_note: The repository description gives qualitative outcome statements. The README mostly describes a hackathon and proposed tasks; results-file contents are unavailable, so no numerical outcomes can be extracted. README instructions are addressed to hackathon participants, not to an AI reader.
record.test_reason: The repository description says the authors confirm Wollschläger et al. (2025): the refusal direction is redundantly encoded in a low-dimensional subspace, causal, but fails as a guardrail. That bears on V4 and, loosely, on V1. The only evidence is this one-line summary. The repo's main work is probe AUC prediction (Level 1) and prompt-edit flipping (Level 2), and no numbers, procedure or results-file contents are available.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors say they confirm Wollschläger et al. (2025): the refusal direction is redundantly encoded in a low-dimensional subspace, and it is causal but fails as a guardrail. The wider project is probing refusal and cyber-harm categories and flipping behaviour with prompt edits on Gemma 4-31B-it and Qwen 3.6-27B.
record.recipe_differences: The repository describes a hackathon probing project, not a reproduction of the original method. The causal procedure and experimental protocol are not specified.

fits_no_version.finding: The direction or probe 'fails as a guardrail': natural-language prompt edits appear to flip refusal probes and/or model behaviour.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-direction-based monitors can be bypassed by minimal natural-language prompt edits.
